name: Graham Healthcare Group
desc:
Palliative Patient Specialist | $19 to $21/hr | Phone-Based Patient Support and Screening, No Sales Expectations
Company: Graham Healthcare Group
Industry: Health Science

What Your Day Will Look Like:
Graham Healthcare Group runs home health, palliative, and hospice care companies. Palliative care helps people with serious illness feel more comfortable, and hospice is end-of-life care. In this role, you're the main contact for patients and families who aren't currently getting one of Graham's services, like patients who were discharged or chose to delay hospice. You'll call them to do screenings and needs assessments over the phone to see what level of care they qualify for, and hold short educational calls to stay in touch with patients and their medical power of attorney. You'll keep patient lists updated in Salesforce, manage the team's Teams chats and emails, answer web inquiries, and work with the Palliative, Home Health, and Hospice teams to get patients care faster. The schedule is Monday through Friday, 8 to 5.

Soft Skills
- Patience and compassion
- Active listening
- Sound judgment
- Juggling several tasks at once
- Clear, caring phone manner
assessment: Expect an assessment that includes typing, personality gaging empathy and multi tasking, and computer literacy
skills:
Actual Minimum Requirements

Education Minimum: High school diploma or GED
Required Experience: None strictly required
Preferred Experience: 2 years of hospice or home health experience and knowledge of medical terminology

Required Skills:
- Active listening
- Customer service skills
- Patience, dependability, and good judgment
- Handling several demands at the same time
- Microsoft Office, including Teams
- Detail-oriented with good time management
- Understanding of HIPAA and confidentiality

This role is ideal for someone who:
- Has worked in hospice, home health, a doctor's office, or as a caregiver
- Is calm and kind with seriously ill patients and worried families
- Wants a steady Monday through Friday daytime schedule
- Is organized and comfortable keeping records in Salesforce or a similar system

Not a Good Fit for someone who:
- Would find end-of-life and serious illness conversations too heavy
- Needs evening or weekend-only hours
- Can't pass a drug screen that includes marijuana
- Struggles to keep detailed records
notes:
Expected Application & Interviewing Process:
1. Submit application
2. Expect an assessment email
3. Watch for an email inviting you to a prescreening
4. Depending on how well the prescreening went, expect an email to schedule an interview
This is an estimated process. A drug screen is part of the background check before you start.

Top 10 Resume Keywords
- Patient advocacy
- Hospice and home health
- Palliative care
- Needs assessment and screening
- Care coordination
- Referral management
- Salesforce
- Medical terminology
- HIPAA compliance
- Customer service

4-5 Interview Questions for this Role:
- Tell us about any experience you have in hospice, home health, or caring for someone with a serious illness.
- How would you start a phone call with a family member whose loved one recently left hospice care?
- How do you keep track of a large list of patients and follow-ups?
- Tell us about a time you supported someone going through a hard situation. What happened, what did you do, and how did it turn out?
- Tell us about a time you worked with several teams to solve a problem. What was the problem, what did you do, and what was the result?
other:
Pay, Shift, Benefits, Background, Drug Test Information, and Career Pathway:
-Pay: $19 to $21/hr. The posting says $21 is a firm cap.
-Shift: Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. The posting doesn't say which time zone, so confirm in the screen.
-Benefits: Health, dental, and vision insurance, 401(k) and pension with a 4% company match, 15 days of PTO, company-paid life and disability insurance, FSA and HSA plans, and 50% off select Purdue and Kaplan courses.
-Equipment Provided: Not stated in the posting. Ask in the interview.
-Felony Friendly?: Case by case
-Drug Test: Required. The pre-employment drug screen includes medical and recreational marijuana.
-Notes: This is a full-time, weekday job with strong benefits, including a pension and 15 days of PTO. It's meaningful work helping seriously ill patients find the right care. Hospice or home health background is preferred but not required. The drug screen includes marijuana, even with a medical card. Training length and camera requirements are not listed.
-Career Pathway: Reasonable inferred path: Palliative Patient Specialist → Senior Patient Specialist → Intake or Care Coordinator → Patient Services Team Lead → Patient Services Manager. This role builds patient advocacy, care coordination, and healthcare intake skills.
